D.t: Charles Booker trails by 13.2 and wins 3% of simulations. Closing it takes about 109,344 voters switching sides, or 218,688 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +21.7 and R +4.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 116,373 votes; Fayette, a projected net 44,935 votes; Franklin, a projected net 4,018 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kenton, R +8.9, 3.7% of the vote; Warren, R +10.3, 2.7% of the vote; Campbell, R +6.0, 2.2% of the vote; Hardin, R +10.6, 2.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Charles Booker runs furthest behind in Laurel, Boone, Oldham. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 40 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.51 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 42 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.44 points; Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 40 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Charles Booker: Immigration voters 15 to 85, Small counties 31 to 69, Voters who can afford daily costs 35 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$310K cash against $2.3M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
